title: Oxycodone for a ureteral stone with senna-docusate: a bowel regimen is ordered

clinical_review.notes: Owner approved 2026-11-16 (#202) the O3 review points of #201 as presented: the case and reference answer, the reviewed reason. The basis is SHM consensus statement 10 as quoted in #201, read by Claude Code in PubMed Central; the owner did not report reading the statement.

story: A 57-year-old man is admitted with a 7 mm left ureteral stone and pain not controlled in the emergency department. He has oxycodone 5 mg by mouth every 4 hours as needed, scheduled acetaminophen, and tamsulosin, and his admission orders include senna-docusate (sennosides 8.6 mg with docusate 50 mg) two tablets at bedtime.

prescriptions.instructions: 5 mg by mouth every 4 hours as needed for pain

prescriptions.drug: docusate sodium 50 MG / sennosides, USP 8.6 MG Oral Tablet

silent.reason: the combination tablet contains senna, a stimulant laxative

reference_answer: No change for this rule: senna-docusate contains senna, a stimulant laxative, so a bowel regimen is ordered. Continue it while he receives oxycodone and track bowel movements.
rationale: A near miss for the bowel regimen rule: docusate is on the order, which alone would not count, but the combination tablet also contains senna. The knowledge base classes the combination product as a stimulant laxative, and the rule must stay silent.

citations.supports: Consensus statement 10: stimulant laxatives such as senna are a bowel regimen; stool softeners alone are not. Read in the PubMed Central full text by Claude Code; owner approved 2026-11-16 (#202).
